html:
The Q'anjob'al are a Maya people of the Cuchumatanes mountains in Huehuetenango, north-western Guatemala, around towns such as Santa Eulalia and San Juan Ixcoy. Their language is close to Akatek and to Popti' (Jakaltek), and more distantly to Chuj. They farm maize and beans on steep slopes, and for generations many worked part of the year on coffee farms on the Pacific coast.

During the civil war the army's scorched-earth campaigns of the early 1980s hit their region hard, and thousands fled to refugee camps in Chiapas, Mexico. Later migrants formed Q'anjob'al communities in the United States, notably in Indiantown, Florida, and Los Angeles.
